title: Agents That Edit Documents: Measuring Agentic PDF Forgery Against a Non-Agentic Control
abstract: arXiv:2609.23953v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents that carry a multi-step computer task through on their own became ordinary tools in the past year, and the same autonomy is available to anyone whose task is harmful. We ask what that means for a relying party -- an insurer, a lender, an auditor -- whose evidence is a filed PDF. AgentForge-Bench measures how reliably an off-the-shelf coding agent, driving one of seven open-weight models with a shell and the stock Python PDF stack, alters one dollar amount, date or address in a real filed financial document from a single sentence of intent, graded by rules rather than by a model. Across 1,750 cells, 1,419 (81.1%) satisfy the verifier, and 808 (46.2%) also survive every stricter filter: visible, localized, typeface-matched, original value gone document-wide. translated_title: 编辑文档的智能体：对照非智能体基线测量智能体式PDF伪造
translated_abstract: 在过去一年中，能够自主完成多步骤计算机任务的AI智能体已成为普通工具，而这种自主能力对于意图作恶的人同样触手可及。我们探讨这对依赖方——如保险公司、贷款机构、审计师——意味着什么，因为他们的证据材料正是一份提交存档的PDF文件。AgentForge-Bench衡量一个现成的编码智能体（驱动七个开放权重模型之一，配备shell和标准Python PDF工具栈）仅凭一句意图描述，篡改真实提交的金融文件中某一金额、日期或地址的可靠程度，评估采用规则判定而非模型打分。在1,750个测试单元中，1,419个（81.1%）通过了验证器，其中808个（46.2%）还通过了所有更严格的过滤条件：视觉上不可察觉、局部修改、字体匹配、且原值在全文中彻底消失。一个不含任何模型的确定性脚本解决了125份文档中的98份；而智能体解决了124份，且没有任何一份是仅脚本能解决而智能体不能的。智能体会错误报告其41%的失败修改（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出AgentForge-Bench基准，首次系统测量了现成AI编码智能体仅凭一句指令即可伪造真实金融PDF文件的能力（81.1%通过验证、46.2%达到不可察觉标准），并证明智能体方法显著超越传统确定性脚本基线。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AgentForge-Bench, a benchmark systematically measuring how readily off-the-shelf coding agents can forge real financial PDFs from a single sentence of intent (81.1% verifier pass rate, 46.2% undetectable), significantly outperforming a deterministic non-agentic script baseline.
